recipe.question: Under the published historical city models, what changes for trips scheduled through the selected corridor when its eligible passenger lanes are limited to 30 km/h for works?
recipe.edge_selection: Among edges referenced by evaluation-window published routes, choose the one with the largest number of distinct scheduled vehicles, at least 100 m length and passenger lane speed above 30 km/h; break ties by source edge ID. The corridor cohort comprises evaluation-window vehicles whose published routes contain that edge. Preserve connectivity and all other lane speeds.
limits: Published real-city models and source data are distinct from raw contemporaneous observations. These are historical scenario experiments, not current traffic forecasts or newly calibrated models.

Departures, routes, vehicle types and mandatory signal programs are preserved within explicit time slices. Empty-network initialization and fixed warm-up are declared; traffic predating the slice is absent.
The counterfactual changes only the selected edge lane speeds; it is hypothetical works, not an observed closure or a guaranteed safety/emission benefit.

Scheduled, departed, arrived, unfinished, undeparted, discarded and teleported vehicles must be accounted for. Paired completed-trip differences exclude censored trips and must report that denominator.
Results on different networks/cohorts cannot establish a city ranking. Raw detector validation availability and model uncertainty remain explicit.
Two original-team cities do not satisfy independent-person third-city final-product qualification.

Native teleports, collisions and legacy signal warnings are retained. Teleport-identified completed trips are excluded from paired comparison, and no forecast readiness is inferred from successful replay.

limits: Published real-city models and source data are distinct from raw contemporaneous observations. These are historical scenario experiments, not current traffic forecasts or newly calibrated models.

Departures, routes, vehicle types and mandatory signal programs are preserved within explicit time slices. Empty-network initialization and fixed warm-up are declared; traffic predating the slice is absent.
The counterfactual changes only the selected edge lane speeds; it is hypothetical works, not an observed closure or a guaranteed safety/emission benefit.

Scheduled, departed, arrived, unfinished, undeparted, discarded and teleported vehicles must be accounted for. Paired completed-trip differences exclude censored trips and must report that denominator.
Results on different networks/cohorts cannot establish a city ranking. Raw detector validation availability and model uncertainty remain explicit.
Two original-team cities do not satisfy independent-person third-city final-product qualification.

Native teleports, collisions and legacy signal warnings are retained. Teleport-identified completed trips are excluded from paired comparison, and no forecast readiness is inferred from successful replay.
A full published road network is loaded with a bounded 06:45-07:10 departure slice; evaluated departures are 07:00-07:10 and the run ends at 07:30.

The publisher fitted demand to mobility matrices and induction-loop counts and hourly fixed-time programs to observed green times. Raw independent traffic observations are not included here; no fresh calibration or independent field validation is claimed.
Original pedestrian connectivity is unsuitable; this recipe uses the publisher motorized route file only.

model_quality.interpretation: Native model events and legacy compatibility warnings require review; no current forecast, physical safety or calibrated intervention claim is admitted. Teleport-identified completed trips are excluded from paired comparison.
